mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen (less negative) for four consecutive weeks, indicating a steady return to in-person work routines that typically pulls weekday retail and recreation visits upward over the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -9.7 to -8.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its monotonic improvement for the full period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility below a low threshold signals households spending markedly less time at home, which frees discretionary time for retail and recreation trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +4.0 percent-change-from-baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 6.6 to 3.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL has dropped below the 4.0 threshold for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility indicates commuters are both traveling and working on-site again, and the combined effect compounds to drive a larger rise in RETAIL_REC than either series would predict alone over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -31.0 to -27.3 and WORKPLACES rose from -9.1 to -8.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than the growth predicted by either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone, or RETAIL_REC declines despite both series improving together.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS dip in t-1w followed by a rebound in t-0w reflects a transient weather or seasonal disruption rather than a structural behavioral shift; once the anomaly clears, outdoor activity substitution effects on RETAIL_REC normalize within one week and produce no lasting directional signal.
candidate_trigger: PARKS swings more than 10 points week-on-week in either direction
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -17.1 to -27.3 then rebounded to -16.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to stabilize or move positively within one week after the PARKS anomaly resolves, or PARKS continues to swing by more than 10 points with no corresponding RETAIL_REC response.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week jump in TRANSIT mobility exceeding a large threshold signals an easing of transit-related restrictions or capacity limits, which mechanically enables more retail and recreation trips over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -31.0 to -27.3, a 3.7 point jump
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the following two weeks despite TRANSIT having jumped more than 3 points, or the TRANSIT jump proves to be a one-week noise spike that reverses.

mechanism_narrative: A gradual decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility toward baseline indicates households are shifting away from essential-only stockpiling behavior toward normal shopping patterns, which correlates with a parallel rise in discretionary RETAIL_REC visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined steadily from 2.3 to 1.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 14 days even as GROCERY_PHARM continues its gradual decline toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The compound effect of falling RESIDENTIAL time-at-home combined with rising WORKPLACES attendance produces a multiplicative boost to RETAIL_REC that exceeds the additive prediction from either trend alone, since both free up and redirect daytime mobility toward commercial areas over a full four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines and WORKPLACES rises concurrently for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.6 to 3.7 while WORKPLACES rose from -9.7 to -8.4 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over 28 days matches or falls below what RESIDENTIAL or WORKPLACES trends individually would predict, despite both conditions holding concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility is unusually depressed relative to its recent average, suppressed outdoor recreation substitutes into indoor retail and recreation visits, causing RETAIL_REC to rise in the subsequent week as people redirect leisure time indoors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points below its trailing 3-week average
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -27.3 in t-1w, well below the prior 3-week average near -16
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop of more than 10 points below its trailing average, or shows no substitution response at all.
